author: Skallywag27
title: RNG and too many “deals” stop this good game from being great.
content:
I have really enjoyed this game. The animations are fluid, the progression is decently paced and the look is very Disney. 
The issues come when the all of the extras start to happen during the later levels and the RNG rears its ugly head. You get a few wins under belt and progress the quests and challenges, get some puzzle pieces, and then you start to lose. Over and over and buying wild cards or the extra 5 cards aren’t a guarantee to win or even get you closer to winning. It just becomes a coin dump to get you frustrated enough to spend real money. 
And the constant offers when the game starts up are way too much. You open the game and there are at least 3-4 bundles or deals or bargains or sales you have to click through before you can even play the game. It’s way too much. 
Overall the game is fun, but it’s much more fun in the early stages when progression doesn’t feel completely halted by the RNG and you aren’t inundated and overwhelmed with deals and bundles and offers before you can start playing.

content: This game is easy to play and can be very fun however I feel it is unfortunately rigged. I played for a while now and spent a lot of money playing hoping I was just getting unlucky hands but noticed a pattern of game play after a while. This game won’t let you play for long without needing to spend coins. The boards become almost impossible to continue without spending coins. If you leave the game for a day or two and come back it will then have cards more in your favor but once you win a hand or two the cards turn back to becoming repetitive and  impossible again where no matter what moves you do you will have to spend coins in order to advance. The amount of coins they charge go higher and higher each time you use them so it makes it extremely expensive after awhile. If you purchase coins you will also notice that your card hands will start becoming repetitive and impossible to beat without spending coins. It will continue like this until your coin balance becomes low again where you will need to buy more to keep playing. The higher your balance of coins is the worse your hands will be I noticed. It’s just not worth it to continue to play I feel especially when the game is not really based on skill level but on what cards they want to decide to give you to advance or not. I wish I didn’t give this app all my time and money. So I don’t recommend it.

title: Don’t download this game unless you’re prepared to get addicted
content:

I’ve deleted it, downloaded it again and, yes, even spent money on it. You absolutely do NOT need to spend money to play, but apparently I have no self-control when Disney and solitaire join forces.



My biggest complaint is how often you’re prompted with offers to buy things. I wish there weren’t so many pop-ups and pushes to spend money, especially since the game is plenty of fun without paying.



Honest review: super fun, super cute, a total time suck and dangerously addictive. I’d give it five stars if I hadn’t somehow let Disney Solitaire talk me into spending actual money on pretend cards.



If you love Disney, download at your own risk.

author: Bruna AvG
title: 1780 Levels Later, I’m Uninstalling
content:
After playing several days in a row and over 1780 levels I am officially uninstalling this game. I’m extremely disappointed with what it became. 

During the Simba’s Magical Friend Event, I literally played EVERY single day, watched EVERY movie night video to get the extra rewards, kept notifications on, opened the game every hour to collect the bonus coins, accumulated over 500,000 coins at some point, completed EVERY plausible mission during the time of the event, upgraded the map two times getting extra 100 stars for each upgrade. And still, after doing all of that, at the end of the event I was missing over 700 stars to get Simba. It is so frustrating spending hours to get something in a game just to realize that after all this work you still have to put money in the game to have a shot at getting it. 

I understand that free to play games need monetization, and I have no problem with optional purchase, I did spend money in this game before. But when someone plays it consistently, complete essentially everything available, spend hours watching adds, doing whatever they can, and STILL not even come close to earning the main reward, it stops feeling rewarding and starts feeling  like the event was designed to push you into spending money.

I genuinely used to enjoy this game, which is why I made it all the way to level 1780. But realizing that all of that time and effort still wasn’t enough to complete an event has completely taken the enjoyment out of it for me.

If you’re planning to play because you want to collect Magical Friends or complete the major events without spending money, be aware that even playing every single day and completing everything you can may still not be enough…

Unfortunately, after all this time I invested, I am done.

author: Alex1626374848487262884
title: After level 4338 I retire
content:
I wanted to keep going. I really did. It’s ALL the same. No
new features unlike the King variant which has had many over time. The levels are all the same recycled layouts. On top of that it’s definitely rigged to make you use wild cards or shuffles at the end the longer you play a session. It’s something I’ve picked up over my many games. The first 5 or so levels of the day you pass with no power ups needed then if you keep going it just coincidentally gets more difficult until you start the next day. Also the “pvp” challenges are always against bots and not real people. It’s rigged against you to lose the higher the rewards are. Making it to such a high level count is a win for me. Adios!
